meaning: A small flat sheet of film holding tiny pictures of many pages. You read it by magnifying it on a special viewer.
clues: It was a way to store information in a small space.
It was a flat sheet of film.
Pages from newspapers, books, or records were shrunk to tiny pictures on it.
You needed a special reader with a lens and a lit screen to see it.
It has ten letters and starts with M. Its name starts with a word for very small.
assumes: A floppy disk stored computer files
An encyclopedia set is a group of printed books

decoys.meaning: A thin plastic disk in a square case. It stored computer files and could be carried around.
A set of books that explain many subjects, in ABC order.
A library cabinet of small drawers holding cards. Each card told you about one book and where to find it.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, the library kept old newspapers on little film sheets. You slid one under the lens and hunted for your page.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: digital archives. Many libraries let you search old newspapers on a screen and zoom in with two fingers.
